# Research Computing Resources

RCpedia documents the Yen cluster, the shared research computing environment run
by the Data, Analytics, and Research Computing (DARC) group at Stanford GSB. It
covers getting access over SSH and JupyterHub, the yen-slurm batch scheduler and
its GPU partition, storage and data transfer, usage limits and data-security
policies, AI coding agents, and per-language guides for Python, R, Julia, Stata,
SAS, Matlab, and optimization solvers.

The Optional section is the DARC blog - an index plus individual posts, newest
first, each tagged with its publication date. Posts are worth reading, but an
older one may refer to software versions, module names, or paths that have since
changed; prefer the sections above when the two disagree.

## Getting Started

- [Status](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/status/index.md): live cluster status, outages, and maintenance windows - check here first if something is broken
- [Yen Servers](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_getting_started/yen-servers/index.md): the Yen cluster - what the nodes are, their specs, and which one to use
- [Access the Yens](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_getting_started/how_access_yens/index.md): who is eligible, SSH access, VPN, and sponsored accounts
- [Jupyter](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_getting_started/jupyter/index.md): JupyterHub web-based notebooks and terminals on yen1-yen5
- [Modules](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_getting_started/modules/index.md): software installed on the Yens and loading specific versions with module
- [Home](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/index.md): map of the rest of the user guide

## Slurm and Batch Jobs

- [Slurm](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/slurm/index.md): the yen-slurm scheduler - writing sbatch scripts, submitting jobs, and checking the queue
- [Migrating From JupyterHub](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/migrating_from_jupyter/index.md): moving a long-running process off JupyterHub onto yen-slurm
- [Job Arrays](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/job_arrays/index.md): running one script over many inputs with Slurm job arrays
- [GPU Slurm Jobs](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/using_gpu/index.md): the yen-slurm gpu partition and requesting GPUs in a job script

## Languages and Software

- [Running Python Interactively](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/python/index.md): running Python interactively on the Yens
- [Python Virtual Environments](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/python_envs/index.md): creating Python virtual environments (venv, Virtualenv, Pipenv) and installing packages
- [Parallel Processing Python](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/parallel_processing_python/index.md): parallelizing Python and capping how many cores a library takes
- [Running R Interactively](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/r/index.md): running R interactively via the module command
- [RStudio](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/rstudio/index.md): using RStudio through JupyterHub
- [Best Practices in R](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/parallel_processing_r/index.md): parallel processing in R - building clusters without oversubscribing shared nodes
- [AI Coding Agents](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/ai_agents/index.md): running AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini) and the Stanford AI API gateway
- [Matlab](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/matlab_interactive/index.md): running Matlab interactively
- [Julia](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/julia/index.md): running Julia interactively
- [SAS](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/sas/index.md): running SAS interactively
- [Stata](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/stata/index.md): running Stata interactively
- [Optimization Software](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/optimization/index.md): licensed Gurobi, Knitro, and AMPL solvers, interactively and in Slurm

## Interactive Sessions and Resource Use

- [Monitor Resource Usage](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/monitor_usage/index.md): checking your own CPU and memory usage with htop and related tools
- [screen](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/screen/index.md): keeping a job running after you log out, and why Slurm is usually the better answer
- [GUI](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/using_gui/index.md): graphical applications via JupyterHub or SSH X-forwarding

## Storage and Data

- [Storage](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/storage/index.md): where research data lives and the quota on each - home 80 GB, project space 1 TB faculty / 200 GB student, ~100 TB shared scratch
- [Data Transfer](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/data_transfer/index.md): moving data to and from the Yens, from small uploads to large transfers
- [File Management](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/file_management/index.md): naming conventions and keeping the file count in a directory manageable
- [Archive](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/archiving/index.md): cleaning up and archiving data when a project wraps up

## Troubleshooting

- [Status](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/status/index.md): live cluster status - check here first before debugging anything else
- [Why isn't JupyterHub Working?](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/jupyter_does_not_work/index.md): JupyterHub will not start or load - browser, access, and quota causes
- [Man-in-the-Middle Warning](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/man_in_middle/index.md): the SSH host key changed warning - what it means and how to clear it
- [Julia on Jupyter](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/julia_on_jupyter/index.md): installing a Julia kernel so Julia appears in JupyterHub

## Beyond the Yens

- [Sherlock](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/sherlock/index.md): Stanford's Sherlock HPC cluster and when to use it instead of the Yens
- [Redivis](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_user_guide/redivis/index.md): Redivis for querying multi-TB datasets, as an alternative to storing them on the Yens

## Policies

- [User Limits](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/user_limits/index.md): CPU, memory, and storage limits on the interactive nodes yen1-yen5 and on JupyterHub
- [Security](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/security/index.md): Stanford data risk levels and whether high risk data (PHI, HIPAA, PII) may go on the Yens
- [Human Subjects Research](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/humanSubjectsResearch/index.md): human subjects data and when your study needs IRB approval
- [Services](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/darc/index.md): DARC services and request forms, including requesting a new project space or more quota
- [Collaborators](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/collaborators/index.md): SUNet ID sponsorship and Yen access for collaborators outside the GSB
- [Workgroups](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/workgroups/index.md): Stanford workgroups, which control Yen logins and project space access
- [Acknowledgements](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/acknowledgements/index.md): how to acknowledge or cite the Yens and the DARC team in publications
- [Leaving GSB](https://rcpedia.stanford.edu/_policies/leavingGSB/index.md): what happens to your SUNet ID, Yen access, and data when you leave GSB
